acceptance of T5, T6, T7, T8 as automated tests
sizes and lab timings of SPEC 7.6 on the core path M0 to M5
a release build succeeds and prints its two reports (open items; numbers in prose)
no-JavaScript run, axe, sizes on every route; reference hashes unchanged

P3-A1.title: Engine phase 3A: Weyl group data, counting, dimension formula
P3-A1.summary: separatingRoots, bipartition, wavePlay, exponentsFromFired, weylOrder, orbitSize, weylDimension, countCompleteGames, legalLayers, with their golden tests and the e8 golden record (fundamental weights and the 56 neighbours), and the cross-check of coxeter_number with the number of wave rounds.
spec: 2.14 (the E8 facts paragraph, for the e8 golden key)
5.7 (phase 3 row; details on coxeter_number and fundamental_orbit_sizes)
deliverables: separatingRoots: positive roots beta with <a, beta^vee> < 0
bipartition: two colour classes or null on an odd cycle
wavePlay: fire one colour class per round from the start; legality of every firing; rounds counted; ends after h rounds from rho on rank >= 2
exponentsFromFired (conjugate partition of the tally), weylOrder = prod (m_i + 1)
orbitSize: play a to the end, J = nodes where the end is zero, |W| / |W_J| (no enumeration)
weylDimension as bigint: M / D along the same word
countCompleteGames by dynamic programming over positions layer by layer, bigint, offered for |W| <= 60000, null above the cap; legalLayers with cap 100000 default

golden tests: exponents, weyl_order, bipartite_colouring, fundamental_orbit_sizes (orbitSize for all; enumerated size where at most 20000), n_reduced_words_w0 and length_distribution where present, all 30 weyl_dimension records including 3875 for E8, e8 fundamental weights via toPopulation and the 56 neighbours via formValue; coxeter_number equals the wave rounds for rank >= 2
acceptance: the phase-3A keys covered and passing (G3)
weylDimension of E8 lambda for 3875 computes in under a second
traps: Exponents come from the tally of fired numbers from rho read sideways (F7); do not compute them from eigenvalues here.
orbitSize takes any position: play it to the end first (5.4).
countCompleteGames must be bigint; 12985968 for D5 fits a number but E6 does not (5.6: offered only for |W| <= 60000, so E6 returns null).

P3-A2.title: Engine phase 3B: heaps, complete games, symbolic play, Cholesky basis, benchmark
P3-A2.summary: heap, heapKey, commutationClassSize, allCompleteGames, symbolicPlay, choleskyBasis, the heaps and pentagon_example.complete_games golden tests, property test 12, and the Vitest benchmark of SPEC 7.6.
golden: (symbolic forms against types[*].positive_roots of the transposed board for T7's acceptance)
deliverables: heap: brick k lands on level 1 + max of the levels of earlier bricks at the same or a joined node; heapKey equal for plays with the same heap
commutationClassSize by dynamic programming over bit masks of bricks laid, bigint
allCompleteGames: every complete legal play from start as an Enumeration of words; works on any board; stops at the cap when plays do not end
symbolicPlay: the linear forms fired as integer coefficient vectors; F6: they are the positive roots of the reversed board
choleskyBasis: upper triangular U with U^T U = B; alpha_1 along the first axis, alpha_2 at pi - pi/m

golden tests: heaps for the six boards (complete_games, distinct_heaps, games_per_heap sorted) and the three minuscule plays (moves, orbit_size via orbit, complete_games); pentagon_example.complete_games = 1230; symbolic forms on every type of rank at most 4 and E6 equal the positive roots of the transposed Cartan matrix
property 12: heap unchanged by exchanging adjacent moves at unjoined nodes; commutationClassSize equal for both words
orbit.bench.ts: the 12-cycle with a chord joining nodes 1 and 7, 2000 positions in Big, median of seven runs, fails above 25 ms
acceptance: heaps and pentagon_example.complete_games covered and passing (G3)
property 12 passing
the benchmark passes on this machine (G3 item of 7.6)
traps: Symbolic forms are roots of the REVERSED board; on B3 the table differs from B3's own positive roots (T7 acceptance).
allCompleteGames on A5 has 292864 plays: respect the cap; the heaps golden uses six small boards.
choleskyBasis is floating point; test U^T U = B to 1e-9, never coordinates.

P3-A7.title: npm run lab: Lighthouse CI or the Playwright fallback of SPEC 7.6
P3-A7.summary: The lab timings command: Lighthouse CI at its current version if it runs under Node 22 within an hour of effort, else the Playwright fallback measuring Largest Contentful Paint, Total Blocking Time and Cumulative Layout Shift on Chromium with the processor slowed four times through a DevTools session, at 360 by 800; thresholds 2.5 s, 200 ms, 0.1; the choice recorded.
owns: site/package.json or root package.json (the lab dependency if Lighthouse CI is chosen; protocol: this dependency only)
deliverables: lab.mjs taking a route list (default: the core path M0 to M5 and the index; from G6 every page) and printing LCP, TBT, CLS per route against the thresholds, exit non-zero on failure
decisions fragment: which tool, why, versions, and the hour spent if Lighthouse CI was abandoned
acceptance: npm run lab runs on the built site and prints the three numbers per route (G3)
a deliberately slow fixture route fails the thresholds (test)
traps: Measure against astro preview, never astro dev.
Processor slowdown must be applied through CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate (4x).

P3-A3.title: Tool T5 Numbers Game Lab
P3-A3.summary: Start chooser (all ones, a fundamental weight, custom), the tape of fired numbers, the tally read sideways into exponents with the product beside the group order, the wave with round count, two games compared with overlaid sorted tapes, and the dimension calculator with exact big integers; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T5 as tests.
deliverables: the six features of SPEC 4 T5 with the lowest-node rule for step and play to the end; big integers shown shortened with exact digits in the table and export

T05.test.ts: exponents, weyl_order and fired_tally for every type; the wave takes coxeter_number rounds on every type of rank at least 2 (A1: a single move and the tool says so); all 30 weyl_dimension entries including 3875 for E8
T05.spec.ts: A3 tally reads (3,2,1) → exponents 1,2,3 → 24; the wave on A3 takes 4 rounds; the dimension calculator on A2 with lambda = (1,1) gives 8; E8 play to the end with the tally and 696729600
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T5 acceptance has a passing test (G3)
E8 play to the end (120 moves) stays on the main thread (under 2000 moves) and completes without a long task
traps: The tally bars are read sideways: the conjugate partition gives the exponents (F7).
Two games compared: the tapes agree after sorting, not in order (F3).
The dimension is a quotient of two products of bigints; never floats.

P3-A4.title: Tool T6 Kaleidoscope
P3-A4.summary: The rank-2 plane for A2, B2, C2, G2 with the two mirrors, the simple roots as normals in the triangular basis of choleskyBasis, the chambers, one lattice point with its numbers (scaled distances) and its population (parallelogram, exact fractions), firing as reflection, placement by buttons and keys as well as drag with snapping, overlays; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T6 as tests.
spec: 3 M2 beat 4 (replaces the static), M4 beat 4
deliverables: the plane with alpha_1 along the positive horizontal axis of length sqrt(2 d_1), alpha_2 of length sqrt(2 d_2) at 120, 135 or 150 degrees counterclockwise; mirrors; chambers; the point as a position a with the two readouts (numbers as scaled distances per 2.4(d); population p = C^{-1} a as the parallelogram and as exact fractions); firing reflects the point and updates both readouts with the line a = Cp; placement by buttons and keys with lattice snapping on drag; overlays: all roots, the orbit, the two lattices

T06.test.ts: for 50 random lattice points per board a = Cp holds in exact rational arithmetic; firing node i changes the numbers as fire says and the population by -a_i e_i; the roots are drawn at the right angles and lengths (ratio sqrt 2 for B2 and C2, sqrt 3 for G2) tested through U^T U = B
T06.spec.ts: the M4 figure (A2, a = (1,1)); keyboard placement; reduced motion
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T6 acceptance has a passing test (G3)
no drag-only action (A-8)
traps: The number on node i is 2/|alpha_i| times the signed distance to mirror i (2.4(d)); the scaling differs between long and short roots.
B2 and C2 are the same board with nodes exchanged; offer both names, draw each in its own numbering (D19).

P3-A5.title: Tool T7 Symbolic Game, LinearForm as MathML, T1 colour-class panel
P3-A5.summary: Two boards side by side: legal play on the left from an all-positive start, letters x_1..x_n on the right with the fired linear forms matched to positive roots of the reversed board; LinearForm.svelte as MathML with the three-engine check of SPEC 7.3 and the span fallback; the colour-class panel of T1 that arrives in phase 3.
spec: 7.3 (Mathematics produced while a tool runs: LinearForm, the MathML [U] check)
deliverables: T07: the two boards; the right board follows the left; each fired entry shown as a linear form (LinearForm) with a side table matching positive roots of the reversed board; at the end every positive root used once

LinearForm.svelte: MathML (<math>, <mi>, <mn>, <mo>, <msub>) with an aria-label; mathml.spec.ts checks rendering in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox (Playwright projects added for this spec only); if an engine fails, switch to HTML spans with aria-label and record it (7.3)
T1 panel: the two colour classes from bipartition, shown by shape and label as well as colour

T07.test.ts: on every type of rank at most 4 and E6 with longest_word the multiset of fired forms equals the positive roots of the transposed Cartan matrix; on B3 the table differs from B3's own positive roots
T07.spec.ts: the B2 game from (x1, x2) fires x1, 2x1 + x2, x1 + x2, x2 (Appendix A.1)
acceptance: SPEC 4 T7 acceptance passes (G3)
the MathML [U] item of 7.3 is settled and recorded (decisions)
traps: Forms are roots of the reversed board (transpose); on B2 the form 2x1 + x2 corresponds to (2,1) of C2, where B2 has (1,2).
Webkit and Firefox browsers must be installed for the MathML check only; keep the main e2e project on Chromium.

P3-A6.title: Tool T8 Weyl Explorer
P3-A6.summary: For the boards with at most 1152 group elements: the layered graph of positions reachable from all ones by legal play, the reader's game as a path, hover and focus showing the position, a shortest word and the separating roots, the counter of complete games, the heap view with the commutation class size, the size rules (dots, sideways scroll, edges only along the game and around the focus above 192 elements), and the SVG snapshot without JavaScript on the larger boards; every acceptance criterion of SPEC 4 T8 as tests.
deliverables: the layered graph via layeredLayout with the widest-layer widths of SPEC 4 T8; the current game as a path driven by a linked T1; hover and focus details; the counter from countCompleteGames (all offered boards have |W| <= 1152 so it runs on the main thread); the heap view as a stack of bricks with commutationClassSize; edges only along the game and around the focus above 192 elements; sideways scroll inside the box; SVG snapshot of the default view produced at build time by the layout code running in Node for the boards above 192 elements

T08.test.ts: layer sizes equal length_distribution and sum to weyl_order for every offered board; top-to-bottom path count equals n_reduced_words_w0; two plays differing by an exchange at unjoined nodes show the same heap; on A3 the 16 games show 8 heaps with games_per_heap
T08.spec.ts: A3 with a linked T1 highlights the path; hovering a vertex shows the word and separating mirrors; the F4 route ships an SVG snapshot without JavaScript
acceptance: every bullet of SPEC 4 T8 acceptance has a passing test (G3)
the F4 default view (1152 elements) renders without a long task and without the worker
traps: Boards offered: A1 to A5, B2 to B4, C2 to C4, D4, F4, G2 only (5.6).
Above 192 group elements draw edges only along the current game and around the focused vertex (4 T8).
The widest layer of A5 has 101 positions; the box scrolls sideways (A-11).
